A dispose of a session waits for a `createSession` of the same session that was requested before it (`AgentService.disposeSession` and `disposeSessionIf`), so it runs after the provider has registered the draft's provisional chat and disposes it. Creation does not offer such a draft to the prewarmer; otherwise its launch would only be discarded by the expiry below. Creation must never dispose its own session through these entry points (it rolls back the provider chat directly), or it would wait on itself.

-A warm launch is the launch the first send would run, started early and kept on the draft's reservation (`IProvisionalSession.earlyLaunch` in `CopilotAgent`). Its session is registered live, so MCP status and sign-in requests reach it, but it is never persisted, listed or announced until the first send completes it exactly as a cold materialization would. When anything fixed at launch has changed by the first send, that send discards it and launches cold. That covers the working directory (always the case for a worktree send), the model or custom agent selection, launch-only tool configuration, plugin or MCP definitions, and the chat's owner. Other client-tool changes are applied with `session.setTools` before claiming the warm session. Turn telemetry reports whether the send used it (`usedPrewarmedSession`) or why it discarded it (`prewarmedSessionDiscardReason`). It is also discarded when the chat is disposed, or after 5 unsent minutes. A runtime torn down underneath it (a client restart, closed-connection recovery or idle release) is forgotten while the reservation stays, and its leftover SDK state is deleted before the next launch. An unsent warm launch is never resumed, because the SDK has saved nothing to resume. A worktree draft never warms: its customization enablement stays pending until the worktree is created on the first send. While the setting is on, the Agents window therefore keeps the isolation choice local until Send: it creates every draft in the picked folder, even when the user picked or inherited a worktree, and its first request sends the picked isolation (and base branch) with the rest of the draft's config as a `SessionConfigChanged`, which marks a worktree pending while the session is still creating. That folder draft warms; a worktree send discards the warm launch and starts cold in the new worktree, and a folder send claims it.

+A warm launch is the launch the first send would run, started early and kept on the draft's reservation (`IProvisionalSession.earlyLaunch` in `CopilotAgent`). Its session is registered live, so MCP status and sign-in requests reach it, but it is never persisted, listed or announced until the first send completes it exactly as a cold materialization would. When anything fixed at launch has changed by the first send, that send discards it and launches cold. That covers the working directory (always the case for a worktree send), the model id (`modelChanged`, or `modelSelected` when the draft was warmed without a model) or custom agent selection, launch-only tool configuration, plugin or MCP definitions, and the chat's owner. A change to only the model's options, such as reasoning effort or context size, is applied with `setModel` before claiming the warm session, unless the launch set per-model capability overrides or GPT-5.6's verbosity, which `setModel` does not reapply; if applying fails, the send launches cold (`modelOptionsFailed`). Other client-tool changes are applied with `session.setTools` before claiming the warm session. Turn telemetry reports whether the send used it (`usedPrewarmedSession`), why it discarded it (`prewarmedSessionDiscardReason`), or why the draft had none (`prewarmSkipReason`: the prewarmer's pending or failed gate, `disabled`, `warmFailed`, `expired`, `released`, or `notRequested`). Both the send and the overlapped turn preparation (`IAgentChats.prepareTurn`) report it, whichever materializes the draft. It is also discarded when the chat is disposed, or after 5 unsent minutes. A runtime torn down underneath it (a client restart, closed-connection recovery or idle release) is forgotten while the reservation stays, and its leftover SDK state is deleted before the next launch. An unsent warm launch is never resumed, because the SDK has saved nothing to resume. A worktree draft never warms: its customization enablement stays pending until the worktree is created on the first send. While the setting is on, the Agents window therefore keeps the isolation choice local until Send: it creates every draft in the picked folder, even when the user picked or inherited a worktree, and its first request sends the picked isolation (and base branch) with the rest of the draft's config as a `SessionConfigChanged`, which marks a worktree pending while the session is still creating. That folder draft warms; a worktree send discards the warm launch and starts cold in the new worktree, and a folder send claims it.

+Both windows create their draft with the model selected in the chat input (`AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService` in the editor window), because the first send selects its model before it runs and discards a launch made with another one (`modelChanged`). A model selected after the draft is created keeps the draft's backend session: replacing it would drop the session-scoped customization choices made for the draft, such as a disabled MCP server, so that send launches cold instead. In the editor window, a draft whose chat model was disposed is retired, so chat input chips that still show it while the widget switches to the next chat cannot recreate a backend for it.
